newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan CPC puts Feb '97 deadline on Indonesia move.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan CPC puts Feb '97 deadline on Indonesia move.

text.p: Taiwan state monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp said on Friday it would abandon a plan to move its No.2 cracker to Indonesia from Taiwan if it could not finalise a site for the plant by February 1997.
"If the site selection problem cannot be solved by February 1997, then we will cancel the move," company president Pan Wen-yen told reporters in Taipei.
Pan did not elaborate on what problems his company was encountering.

Other officials explained privately that the economic value of the plant, which is now in Taiwan's southern Kaohsiung, would diminish over time and that the point at which a move would be uneconomic was looming.
Chinese Petroleum had said in June it was considering alternative proposals to build a new naphtha cracker in Indonesia rather than moving the No.2 cracker.
The No.2 cracker is currently out of service.
